questions.q: What does the summary's principle of New Economics ask you to include when judging a purchase?
a: The non-monetary costs, like time and stress
The resale value after a few years
The opinions of friends and family
The environmental cost of shipping
questions.why: Lesson 1 says New Economics counts hidden costs such as the effort needed to earn and maintain something.

questions.q: How does the summary describe the Amish approach to new technology?
a: Test and question it before deciding to adopt it
Reject every modern device on principle
Adopt new tools as soon as they appear
Leave the decision to community elders only
questions.why: Lesson 1 explains that the Amish evaluate new products against their values, adopting only what passes.

questions.q: What does Newport call pastimes like scrolling social media and mindless binge-watching?
a: Low-quality recreation
High-quality leisure
Passive recovery
Digital downtime
questions.why: Lesson 2 contrasts high-quality leisure with low-quality recreation such as social media and absent-minded binging.

questions.q: What is solitude deprivation, according to the summary?
a: A lack of time alone with your own thoughts
A fear of being without a phone
A loss of interest in hobbies
A habit of working late every night
questions.why: Lesson 3 says younger generations miss out on solitude, which is essential for processing emotions.

questions.q: Why does the summary warn against relying on quick fixes and life hacks?
a: They rarely create lasting change over time
They cost more than professional help
They make screen time feel more rewarding
They only work for people under thirty
questions.why: Lesson 3 says quick fixes may start a habit but do not support sustainable, long-term change.
